title: Liters and Gallons: Fuel Tank Sizing Across Regions
h1: Litres and gallons — reading fuel tank capacities without surprises
description: A 15-gallon US tank is not 15 UK gallons. Here is how vehicle fuel-tank capacities convert, and where the US-vs-UK gallon confusion hits hardest.

author.name: The Turbo Unit Converter engineering desk

hero: 1 US gallon = 3.785 L. 1 UK gallon = 4.546 L. The 20% gap is the same one that ruins fuel-economy comparisons.
body: The US gallon and the UK (Imperial) gallon share a name and nothing else. A 15-gallon fuel tank on a US pickup holds 56.8 L; the same-sized tank on a UK van rated 15 (Imperial) gallons holds 68.2 L. The 20% difference has caught out fleet managers, importers and every backpacker filling up abroad.

> 1 US gallon = 3.785411784 L (exact)
> 1 Imperial gallon = 4.54609 L (exact)
> 1 US gal = 0.8327 UK gal
> 1 L = 0.2642 US gal = 0.2200 UK gal

US: gallons everywhere. UK: litres at the pump, gallons in casual fuel-economy talk. Canada: litres exclusively since 1979. Australia: litres. EU: litres. Japan: litres. Only the US retains gallons on the pump.
## Worked example — a 60 L rental car in the US

You land in Los Angeles, rent a car with a 60 L tank (16 US gal) and fill up in Nevada for $3.50/gal. 60 L / 3.785 = 15.85 US gal × $3.50 = $55.48. If the same tank were labelled in UK gal you would expect 60/4.546 = 13.2 gal — the mismatch of 2.65 gal at $3.50 is $9.28 you did not budget.

Marine and aviation fuel is often quoted in US gallons regardless of country, because the industry standardised on US convention. A 100-gallon aviation fuel order in the UK is 378.5 L, not 454.6 L. Always confirm at the fuel truck.
Multiply US gal by 3.785 for L. Multiply UK gal by 4.546 for L. The two gallons differ by 20%. Aviation defaults to US gal worldwide.

faqs.q: Which gallon is the US gallon based on?
faqs.a: The Queen Anne wine gallon of 1707 — 231 cubic inches exactly. The UK abandoned it in 1824 for the Imperial gallon; the US kept it.

faqs.q: How many litres in a barrel of oil?
faqs.a: 1 US oil barrel = 158.987 L = 42 US gal. This is different from a US liquid barrel (119.24 L) or a UK beer barrel (163.66 L).

faqs.q: Does Canada use US or UK gallons?
faqs.a: Neither in practice — Canada switched to litres in 1979. Legacy references are UK gallons (a Canadian 'gallon' historically = 4.546 L).
